about: Tool-definition facts both MCP servers state alike. Generated from apps/site by node scripts/check-mcp-accuracy.js --write-definitions; checked there, by scripts/check-mcp-tool-parity.js, and by the PyPI suite (test/test_tool_definitions.py).
instructions:
Designesy (designesy.org) publishes a design-system contract and rule-based engines that check web pages and design files against it. Typical uses: checking the design quality of web UI, including AI-generated UI, before it ships, and catching inconsistency and generic AI patterns ('slop'). The tools fall into seven groups.
Score a page: designesy_score, the full contract audit (0-100 and A-F).
Check a design file: designesy_tokens_score (a DTCG token file) and designesy_motion_score (a Lottie file). designesy_a11y_score returns the WCAG 2.2 AA checks with a Playwright and axe-core script to run locally; it scans nothing itself.
Check a site's own system: designesy_drift_score (drift in its tokens), designesy_readiness_score (machine-readable files for AI tools) and designesy_guardrails (a token file, lint config, agent rules and DESIGN.md generated from its tokens).
Watch over time: designesy_monitor_score (drift against earlier snapshots passed as history; can send an alert email when given an address).
Compare two sites: designesy_compare (their tokens diffed).
Combine: designesy_report (score, drift and readiness in one composite grade).
Reference: designesy_contract (the contract JSON), designesy_catalog (the published packages) and designesy_design_review (a critique rubric); designesy_llms_txt, designesy_llms_full_txt, designesy_agent_json and designesy_skill_md return published documents. Rubric and documents return as reference data only.
Scores come from fixed rules applied to the page or file: no language model takes part, so the same input gives the same verdict. The page engines behind score, drift, readiness, guardrails, monitor, compare and report cache each result for about 24 hours. Tools that read a URL refuse non-http(s) URLs, localhost and private IP addresses. An error from a page, file or engine that cannot be reached or read says whether one retry can help.

descriptions.designesy_catalog: List the 24 packages Designesy publishes (contracts, kits, labs, reviews and tools), each with its version, status, and human and machine URLs. Use this when you need to see what Designesy publishes before reading one item. When not to use: for the design-system contract itself, use designesy_contract; for the org's discovery manifest, use designesy_agent_json. Behaviour: reads https://www.designesy.org/open.json, cached for 5 minutes by this server; takes no parameters. If designesy.org cannot be reached, the error says whether a retry can help. Returns JSON: { package_count, packages[{ id, kind, number, title, version, status, lede, human_url, machine_url }], machine_exports[], standing_rules[], catalog_version, updated, identity, thesis, public_url }.
descriptions.designesy_contract: Get the Designesy design-system contract: its top-level sections such as colors, motion, typography, takt, cadence, acoustic, components, accessibility and verification. Use this when you need the contract's actual values (token names and values, motion timings, accessibility rules) to build, check or cite a design. When not to use: for a pass/fail score of a live page, use designesy_score; for the same rules as an agent skill file, use designesy_skill_md. Behaviour: reads https://www.designesy.org/contracts/design-system.json, cached for 5 minutes by this server. With no arguments it returns the whole contract, about 104 KB (roughly 26k tokens). To return less, pass sections, a list of top-level keys such as ["motion", "colors"]: the result holds id, version and only those keys. section (one key) is the older form and returns { section, data }. Both take only the contract's top-level keys, listed in the parameter's enum; an unknown key returns an error that lists every valid key. Returns JSON: the contract object, or the slice asked for.
descriptions.designesy_design_review: Get the Designesy Design Review rubric for a qualitative critique: eight dimensions (Purpose, Clarity, Context, Inclusion, System coherence, Durability, Delight, Responsibility), the output format, the verification checklist, anti-patterns and rationalizations, from the published Design Review kit. Use this when a design needs a structured, holistic critique rather than a numeric score. When not to use: for a deterministic score of a live page, use designesy_score. Behaviour: reads https://www.designesy.org/kits/design-review.json, cached for 5 minutes by this server, and returns it as reference data; it evaluates nothing. The kit's copy-ready review prompt is left out; kit_prompt_url is the page where a person can read it. artifact, purpose, context and rules are optional and are only recorded in inputs (rules defaults to the current contract version). Returns JSON: { kind: "review_rubric", source_url, note, inputs (only when one is passed), kit { id, title, version, status, purpose, quality_bar, permission }, when_to_use[], required_inputs[], dimensions[8] { num, title, desc }, output_format[], verification_checklist[], anti_patterns[], rationalizations[], kit_prompt_url, kit_prompt_note, omitted_fields[] }.
descriptions.designesy_skill_md: Get the Designesy SKILL.md: the design-system contract written as an agent skill file in markdown (tokens, rules, anti-patterns and verification), for a person to save into a project's skills folder or a system prompt so a coding agent builds UI to the contract. Use this when the user wants the contract in that form; it is about the design rules, not about Designesy as an org, and runs to about 31,000 characters. When not to use: for the contract's raw values as JSON, use designesy_contract; for an overview of Designesy, use designesy_llms_txt; for a score, use designesy_score. Behaviour: Takes no parameters; reads the file from www.designesy.org, cached for 5 minutes by this server. Any section written as steps or a prompt for an AI agent is replaced by a one-line marker and named in omitted_sections. Returns JSON: { kind: "published_document", source_url, media_type: "text/markdown", note, omitted_sections[], content }.
descriptions.designesy_agent_json: Get the Designesy agent discovery document (/.well-known/agent.json): the org's identity, authority, discovery endpoints, package index, machine exports, permission policy, contact and citation templates, as JSON. Use this when a program or integration needs those facts as structured fields; the result is about 13,000 characters. When not to use: for the package list alone, use designesy_catalog; for a prose overview, use designesy_llms_txt or designesy_llms_full_txt; for the design rules, use designesy_contract. Behaviour: Takes no parameters; reads the file from www.designesy.org, cached for 5 minutes by this server. Any field written as steps for an AI agent (such as ingest.steps) is removed and its path listed in omitted_fields. Returns JSON: { kind: "published_document", source_url, media_type: "application/json", note, omitted_fields[], document }.
descriptions.designesy_llms_txt: Get the Designesy /llms.txt brief: a short plain-text overview of what Designesy is, its canonical links, topics, published packages, machine exports, standing rules and contact. Use this when you know little about Designesy and want the cheapest orientation, about 7,000 characters. When not to use: for more depth in prose, use designesy_llms_full_txt (about 14,000 characters); for the same facts as structured JSON (endpoints, permission policy, citation templates), use designesy_agent_json; for the design rules themselves, use designesy_contract or designesy_skill_md. Behaviour: Takes no parameters; reads the file from www.designesy.org, cached for 5 minutes by this server. Any section written as steps for an AI agent (such as the ingest steps) is replaced by a one-line marker and named in omitted_sections. Returns JSON: { kind: "published_document", source_url, media_type: "text/plain", note, omitted_sections[], content }.
descriptions.designesy_llms_full_txt: Get the Designesy /llms-full.txt brief: the long plain-text overview, with authority, discovery endpoints, topics, every published package with its links, standing rules and anti-patterns. Use this when the short brief is not enough and prose suits the task better than JSON; it is about 14,000 characters. When not to use: for a quick orientation, use designesy_llms_txt (about 7,000 characters); for structured fields, use designesy_agent_json; for the design rules themselves, use designesy_contract or designesy_skill_md. Behaviour: Takes no parameters; reads the file from www.designesy.org, cached for 5 minutes by this server. Any section written as steps or a prompt for an AI agent (such as the ingest protocol and the paste-ready agent prompt) is replaced by a one-line marker and named in omitted_sections. Returns JSON: { kind: "published_document", source_url, media_type: "text/plain", note, omitted_sections[], content }.
descriptions.designesy_score: Score a live web page against the Designesy design contract with the 44-check rule engine: a 0-100 score, an A-F grade, and each check's verdict and remediation. Use this when a website or AI-built UI needs a numeric, repeatable audit (tokens, motion, accessibility, cadence, takt, typography, copywriting). When not to use: for a token file, use designesy_tokens_score; for a Lottie file, designesy_motion_score; for drift within a site's own tokens, designesy_drift_score; for a qualitative critique, designesy_design_review. Behaviour: the engine at www.designesy.org reads the page and its stylesheets and caches the result for about 24 hours per URL and scope. Checks that need a live browser return MANUAL and checks that do not apply return SKIP; neither counts toward the score. The score subtracts the slop deduction, itemized in slop: generic, template-like patterns (an overused font family, for example), up to 5 points each and 20 in all. A page the engine cannot read (blocked, behind a login, timed out) returns score null with unreachable true and the reason, not an error. format selects the output: designesy (default, the engine's JSON), canonical, google, or review (a markdown report). Errors: a timeout, HTTP 5xx or HTTP 429 (the score engine allows 100 scores an hour per address) is worth one retry; HTTP 400 (not a public http(s) URL) is final. Returns JSON described by the output schema.
descriptions.designesy_tokens_score: Validate one design token file against the W3C Design Tokens Community Group format (DTCG 2025.10, the first stable version) with the tokens contract's ten checks (t01-t10): a $schema pointing at designtokens.org, groups, $type and $value on every token, structured colors (colorSpace and components, not bare hex), standard types, namespaced custom types, dimension units, a nested naming hierarchy, and no pre-2025.10 patterns. Use this when you have a tokens.json or any DTCG export and need to know whether it is well formed. When not to use: for a whole live site rather than its token file, use designesy_score; for drift in a site's CSS tokens, use designesy_drift_score. Behaviour: pass url (the file is read from that address) or dtcg_file (the JSON text); if both are given, dtcg_file is used. No browser. Score: PASS=1, WARN=0.5, FAIL=0, SKIP is not scored; points / scored checks x 100. Errors: a timeout, HTTP 429 or 5xx from the file's host is worth one retry; a private or non-http(s) URL, a host name that does not resolve, a 404, or a reply that is not a JSON object is final; HTTP 401 or 403 needs the user (pass the file's contents as dtcg_file instead). Returns JSON described by the output schema: score, grade, the four counts (pass_count, fail_count, warn_count, skip_count), scoring and checks[{ id, name, status, detail }].
descriptions.designesy_a11y_score: Get the Designesy WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility kit: the contract's eleven checks (a01-a11) and a ready-to-run Playwright test that scans a URL with axe-core 4.13.0 and prints a score. Use this when a page needs an accessibility audit and a browser test can run locally (npm i -D @axe-core/playwright). When not to use: for a full design-contract score of a live page, use designesy_score. Behaviour: this tool scans nothing; axe-core needs a real browser, so every check comes back PENDING_EXECUTION and the score comes from running the script. url is written into the script and is not fetched here; ruleset picks the axe-core tag (default wcag22aa); config is JSON written into the script as an axe.configure() call. Errors: config that is not valid JSON is final (correct it and call again). Returns JSON described by the output schema: checks[{id (a01-a11), name, status: "PENDING_EXECUTION"}], playwright_script, install_command and run_command.
descriptions.designesy_motion_score: Validate one Lottie animation file against the Designesy motion contract: its ten checks (m01-m10), drawn from the Lottie spec v1.0.1 and the Designesy Ten Non-Negotiable Motion Standards, each PASS, FAIL, WARN or SKIP under the contract's own name: m01 the top-level animation object (layer contents are not validated, so a clean file returns SKIP), m02 required fields (v, fr, ip, op, w, h, layers), m03 no deprecated 4.x Bodymovin version, m04 a markers array, m05 a meta object, m06 a reduced-motion path, m07 keyframe easing (linear, ease and ease-in fail), m08 duration within 300 ms (longer is WARN), and m09 and m10 SKIP (they concern the embedding page). Use this when a motion asset must be well formed and carry reduced-motion support. When not to use: for the motion CSS of a whole site, use designesy_score. Behaviour: pass url (read from that address) or lottie_file (the JSON text); if both are given, lottie_file is used. No browser. Score: PASS=1, WARN=0.5, FAIL=0, SKIP is not scored; points / scored checks x 100. Errors: a timeout, HTTP 429 or 5xx from the file's host is worth one retry; a private or non-http(s) URL, an unresolvable host, a 404, or a reply that is not a JSON object is final; HTTP 401 or 403 needs the user (pass the file's contents as lottie_file). Returns JSON described by the output schema.
descriptions.designesy_drift_score: Score a live page for AI-generated UI drift: twelve checks (d01-d12) on its CSS for the four drift failure modes: token fabrication (var() references, with no fallback, to custom properties declared nowhere), within-session drift (spacing, color and radius value variance), between-session amnesia (inconsistent font stacks, shadows and transitions), and silent breaking changes (z-index chaos, alias chains that end in an undeclared property). Use this when a site, especially an AI-built one, may be drifting off its own declared tokens. When not to use: for the full 44-check contract score, use designesy_score; for a token file's format, use designesy_tokens_score; for drift over time against earlier runs, use designesy_monitor_score. Behaviour: the engine at www.designesy.org reads the page, its <style> blocks, linked stylesheets and style attributes, and caches the result for about 24 hours per URL. No browser. Errors: a timeout, HTTP 5xx or HTTP 429 (the drift engine allows 50 scans an hour per address) is worth one retry; HTTP 400 (not a public http(s) URL) is final; a page the engine could not fetch is worth one retry, after which it needs the user: the page may block automated requests or need a login, or the URL may be mistyped. Returns JSON described by the output schema.
descriptions.designesy_readiness_score: Score a site for design-system AI readiness: ten probes (r01-r10) of its origin for machine-readable files: a DTCG token file, llms.txt, agent.json, an MCP endpoint answering tools/list, DESIGN.md, token $description, a component schema, sitemap.xml, robots.txt, and Open Graph and Twitter meta. Use this when you need to know whether AI tools can find and read a design system, rather than how the page is designed. When not to use: for the contract score of the page, use designesy_score; for drift in its tokens, use designesy_drift_score. Behaviour: the engine at www.designesy.org requests each path on the URL's origin and caches the result for about 24 hours per URL. No browser. Errors: a timeout, HTTP 5xx or HTTP 429 (the readiness engine allows 50 scans an hour per address) is worth one retry; HTTP 400 (not a public http(s) URL) is final; a page the engine could not fetch is worth one retry, after which it needs the user: the page may block automated requests or need a login, or the URL may be mistyped. Returns JSON described by the output schema.
descriptions.designesy_guardrails: Generate a build-contract bundle for AI coding agents from a live page's :root custom properties: tokens (a DTCG token file), lintConfig (a Stylelint config), agentRules (AGENTS.md rules with a token allowlist), componentContract (allowed prop patterns), antiPatterns (fabricated tokens included) and designMd (a DESIGN.md: YAML front matter and a markdown body). Use this when a design system must become the files AI agents read and the lint that enforces them. When not to use: for a contract score, use designesy_score; for token-file validation, use designesy_tokens_score; for drift, use designesy_drift_score. Behaviour: the engine at www.designesy.org reads the page and its stylesheets and caches the result for about 24 hours per URL. No browser. The full bundle grows with the number of tokens a site declares: about 7 KB to about 530 KB of JSON on the 26 sites measured (about 110 KB for designesy.org). To trim it, pass parts, a list of bundle file names such as ["designMd"]: the result keeps score, grade, counts and checks, and its bundle holds only those files, in the order asked. Valid parts: tokens, lintConfig, agentRules, componentContract, antiPatterns, designMd. Errors: a timeout, HTTP 5xx or HTTP 429 (the guardrails engine allows 50 bundles an hour per address) is worth one retry; HTTP 400 (not a public http(s) URL) is final; a page the engine could not fetch is worth one retry, after which it needs the user: the page may block automated requests or need a login, or the URL may be mistyped. Returns JSON described by the output schema.
descriptions.designesy_monitor_score: Score one monitoring run of a live page: the twelve drift checks (d01-d12) plus ten governance checks (m01-m10), most of them comparing this run with the snapshots passed in history: drift since the baseline, the 3-run trend, new and resolved violations, score degradation, token-set changes, the contract version, and whether an alert was delivered. Use this when a design system is watched over time: each call is one run, and the caller keeps the snapshots (pass each run's currentSnapshot back in history, oldest first). When not to use: for a single point-in-time drift check, use designesy_drift_score; for a contract score, use designesy_score. Behaviour: nothing is scheduled or stored by this tool. The engine at www.designesy.org reads the page and caches the result for about 24 hours per URL and history. Side effect: when email is given, an alert fires (it needs a non-empty history) and a Resend key is configured on www.designesy.org, an HTML alert email goes to that address; a repeat of the same alerts within an hour is suppressed only per server instance, so a repeated call can send another. Errors: a timeout, HTTP 5xx or HTTP 429 (the monitor engine allows 50 runs an hour per address) is worth one retry; HTTP 400 (not a public http(s) URL) is final; a page the engine could not fetch is worth one retry, after which it needs the user: the page may block automated requests or need a login, or the URL may be mistyped. Returns JSON described by the output schema.
descriptions.designesy_compare: Diff the design tokens of two live pages: reads both, extracts their :root custom properties, and reports tokens added (in A, not B), removed (in B, not A), likely renamed (name distance 2 or less), changed in value, scale size changes (spacing, radius, color), contrast change for shared color tokens, structure (counts and categories), and the score difference (designesy_score on both). Use this when you need to know what changed between two design systems, or how one differs from a reference. When not to use: for drift within one site, use designesy_drift_score; for one site over time, use designesy_monitor_score. Behaviour: the engine at www.designesy.org reads both pages and caches the result for about 24 hours per URL pair; the two URLs must differ. No browser. Errors: a timeout, HTTP 5xx or HTTP 429 (the compare engine allows 30 comparisons an hour per address) is worth one retry; HTTP 400 (not a public http(s) URL) is final; a page the engine could not fetch is worth one retry, after which it needs the user: the page may block automated requests or need a login, or the URL may be mistyped. Returns JSON described by the output schema.
descriptions.designesy_report: Build one design-intelligence report for a live page: runs the score (44-check), drift (12-check) and readiness (10-check) engines and weights them into a composite: score x 0.5 + drift x 0.3 + readiness x 0.2. Use this when one holistic verdict is wanted instead of three separate calls, or to share a result. When not to use: for one engine's result alone, use designesy_score, designesy_drift_score or designesy_readiness_score. Behaviour: the engines at www.designesy.org each read the page, and the result is cached for about 24 hours per URL. The full result is large: about 75 to 100 KB of JSON on the ten sites measured, because it carries each engine's whole result beside the merged check list. detail "summary" keeps the composite, the totals, each engine's score, grade and counts, and only the checks and synthesis entries that did not PASS: about 4 to 31 KB on the same sites. Hosts that support MCP Apps (io.modelcontextprotocol/ui) show an interactive dashboard; appUrl opens it in a browser. Errors: a timeout, HTTP 5xx or HTTP 429 (the report engine allows 20 reports an hour per address) is worth one retry; HTTP 400 (not a public http(s) URL) is final; a page the engine could not fetch is worth one retry, after which it needs the user: the page may block automated requests or need a login, or the URL may be mistyped. Returns JSON described by the output schema.

sections.description: Optional: the top-level keys to return, for example ["motion", "colors"]. The result holds id, version and only these keys. Omit for the whole contract.

section.description: Optional, older form: one top-level key, for example "motion"; returns { section, data }. Prefer sections.

artifact.description: Optional: the URL or a short description of the design to review, for example "https://example.com/pricing".

purpose.description: Optional: what the design is meant to make possible, for example "let a visitor compare plans and start a trial".

context.description: Optional: audience, device, environment and constraints, for example "first-time visitors on mobile, slow networks".

rules.description: Optional: the governing rules or contract version, for example "WCAG 2.2 AA and the team style guide". Defaults to the current Designesy contract version.

url.description: The page to score, for example "https://example.com/". Defaults to https://www.designesy.org/.

format.description: Output format, for example "canonical". designesy (the default): the engine's JSON. canonical: the review-findings.json schema. review: a markdown report. google: findings and a summary in the design.md linter's shape.

scope.description: Scoring scope, for example "universal". contract: every check counts absence against the site. universal: optional features and Designesy-specific token checks return SKIP when absent. Omit to auto-detect: contract for designesy.org, universal for every other site.

url.description: URL of a DTCG token file (JSON), for example "https://example.com/tokens.json". Use this or dtcg_file.

dtcg_file.description: The token file's JSON as a string, for example "{\"color\": {\"ink\": {\"$type\": \"color\", \"$value\": {\"colorSpace\": \"srgb\", \"components\": [0, 0, 0]}}}}". Used instead of url when both are given.

url.description: The page the generated script will scan, for example "https://example.com/". Written into the script; not fetched by this tool.

ruleset.description: The axe-core tag the script runs, for example "wcag21aa". Default wcag22aa.

config.description: Optional JSON, as a string, for an axe.configure() call in the script, for example "{\"rules\": [{\"id\": \"color-contrast\", \"enabled\": false}]}". Omit for the standard WCAG 2.2 AA run.

url.description: URL of a Lottie JSON file, for example "https://example.com/hero.json". Use this or lottie_file.

lottie_file.description: The Lottie JSON as a string, for example "{\"v\": \"5.12.0\", \"fr\": 60, \"ip\": 0, \"op\": 18, \"w\": 100, \"h\": 100, \"layers\": []}". Used instead of url when both are given.

url.description: The page to scan for drift, for example "https://example.com/". Defaults to https://www.designesy.org/.
A page on the site to probe, for example "https://example.com/". Defaults to https://www.designesy.org/.
The page whose tokens to turn into the bundle, for example "https://example.com/". Defaults to https://www.designesy.org/.

parts.description: Optional: the bundle files to return, for example ["designMd"] or ["tokens", "lintConfig"]. Omit for the whole bundle.

url.description: The page to monitor, for example "https://example.com/". Defaults to https://www.designesy.org/.

email.description: Optional: an address for the alert email, for example "design-team@example.com". Mail is sent only when an alert fires and a Resend key is configured on www.designesy.org; without an address, alerts appear only in the result.

history.description: Optional: earlier runs' currentSnapshot objects, oldest first, for example [{"timestamp": "2026-10-01T09:00:00.000Z", "score": 92, "grade": "A", "tokensExtracted": 120, "checks": [...]}]. Omit for a first run, which sets the baseline.

urlA.description: The first page, for example "https://example.com/" (the design system under review).

urlB.description: The second page, for example "https://www.designesy.org/" (a reference); it must differ from urlA.

url.description: The page to report on, for example "https://example.com/".

detail.description: Optional, for example "summary". "full" (the default) returns everything; "summary" returns the composite, the totals, each engine's score, grade and counts, and only the checks that did not PASS.

designesy_score.description: One score result. Which fields appear depends on format and on the server: no field is required, and fields not listed here may appear.

ok.description: format designesy from the engine: true when the engine ran.

score.description: format designesy: weighted score 0-100 after the slop deduction; null when the page could not be read.

grade.description: Letter grade A-F; null when the page could not be read.

scope.description: The scoring scope the engine applied.

contractVersion.description: The design contract version scored against (engine JSON).

checks.description: Every check with its verdict; engine JSON also carries remediation and weight.

categoryScores.description: Per category: score, weight and counts.

slop.description: The slop deduction: generic, template-like patterns found on the page (findings with id S1-S12, label, instances, evidence and deduction) and total, the points subtracted from the score (at most 5 per pattern, 20 in all).

receipt.description: Reproducibility receipt: subject, retrieved_at, contract and engine versions, scope, and a digest of the verdict set (null when nothing was measured).

unreachable.description: true when the page could not be read; score and grade are then null.

url.description: The scored URL (the stdio package's designesy format).

contract_version.description: The stdio package's designesy format: the contract version scored against.

summary.description: Counts, score and grade: format canonical and google, and the stdio package's designesy format (score 0-1, score_percent 0-100).

note.description: The stdio package's designesy format: how the result was produced.

engine.description: Present when the stdio package's offline engine produced the result: which checks it ran and did not run.

findings.description: format canonical and google: the checks as findings.

verdict.description: format canonical: pass, needs-changes, fail or not-scored.

markdown.description: format review: the engine's markdown report, the same text as the content block.

designesy_tokens_score.description: The tokens contract's ten checks (t01-t10) on one DTCG token file.

contract_id.description: The contract the checks come from.

url.description: The token file's URL, or (inline dtcg_file).

score.description: PASS=1, WARN=0.5, FAIL=0; SKIP is not scored; points / scored checks x 100.

grade.description: Letter grade from the score: A>=90, B>=80, C>=70, D>=60, F below.

checks.description: One entry per check (t01-t10), named by the contract.

designesy_a11y_score.description: The accessibility contract's checks and a Playwright + axe-core script to run locally; nothing is scanned by this tool.

contract_id.description: The contract the checks come from.

url.description: The URL written into the script.

ruleset.description: The axe-core tag the script filters on.

checks.description: The contract's checks (a01-a11), each PENDING_EXECUTION until the script runs.

playwright_script.description: A Playwright test that runs axe-core on url and prints a score.

designesy_motion_score.description: The motion contract's ten checks (m01-m10) on one Lottie file.

contract_id.description: The contract the checks come from.

url.description: The Lottie file's URL, or (inline lottie_file).

score.description: PASS=1, WARN=0.5, FAIL=0; SKIP is not scored; points / scored checks x 100.

grade.description: Letter grade from the score: A>=90, B>=80, C>=70, D>=60, F below.

checks.description: One entry per check (m01-m10), named by the contract.

designesy_drift_score.description: The drift engine's twelve checks (d01-d12) on one page.

scope.description: universal turns d01 into SKIP when the page declares no custom properties.

score.description: PASS=1, WARN=0.5, FAIL=0 over the checks that are not SKIP.

grade.description: Letter grade from the score: A>=90, B>=80, C>=70, D>=60, F below.

designesy_readiness_score.description: The readiness engine's ten probes (r01-r10) of one origin.

score.description: PASS=1, WARN=0.5, FAIL=0 over all ten checks.

grade.description: Letter grade from the score: A>=90, B>=80, C>=70, D>=60, F below.

designesy_guardrails.description: The build-contract bundle generated from one page's :root custom properties, with six emission checks (g01-g06).

grade.description: Letter grade from the score: A>=90, B>=80, C>=70, D>=60, F below.

parts.description: Present when parts was passed: the bundle files returned, in the order asked.

bundle.description: tokens (DTCG token file), lintConfig (Stylelint config), agentRules (AGENTS.md text), componentContract, antiPatterns and designMd (DESIGN.md text); with parts, only the named files.

designesy_monitor_score.description: One monitor run: the twelve drift checks on the page and ten governance checks (m01-m10) against the history passed in.

score.description: Governance health from the monitor checks, not design quality.

grade.description: Letter grade from the score: A>=90, B>=80, C>=70, D>=60, F below.

currentSnapshot.description: This run as a snapshot (timestamp, score, grade, tokensExtracted, checks); pass it back in history next time.

baseline.description: The first snapshot in history, or null.

previous.description: The last snapshot in history, or null.

alerts.description: The alert conditions this run raised.

emailAlert.description: Present when an email was given and alerts fired: attempted, delivered, recipient and error.

designesy_compare.description: The diff of two pages' :root custom properties, with eight diff checks (c01-c08).

grade.description: Letter grade from the score: A>=90, B>=80, C>=70, D>=60, F below.

added.description: Tokens in A and not in B.

removed.description: Tokens in B and not in A.

renamed.description: Likely renames (name distance 2 or less): from, to, distance, valueA, valueB.

scaleDiff.description: Spacing, radius and color scale sizes in A and B.

structureDelta.description: Token counts and category distribution in A and B.

contrastDrift.description: Contrast ratio change for shared color tokens.

scoreDelta.description: Both pages' designesy_score scores and grades and their difference; null when either could not be scored.

designesy_report.description: The composite report: the score, drift and readiness engines run on one URL and weighted into one grade.

compositeScore.description: score x 0.5 + drift x 0.3 + readiness x 0.2, re-weighted when an engine returned no score.

compositeGrade.description: Letter grade from the score: A>=90, B>=80, C>=70, D>=60, F below.

score.description: The score engine's result (with detail summary: its single values only).

drift.description: The drift engine's result (with detail summary: its single values only).

readiness.description: The readiness engine's result (with detail summary: its single values only).

checks.description: Every engine's checks, each tagged with engine; with detail summary, only those that did not PASS.

synthesis.description: rp01-rp08: whether each engine ran and the composite holds; with detail summary, only those that did not PASS.

appUrl.description: The interactive dashboard for this URL in a browser.

omitted.description: With detail summary: how many PASS rows were left out, and what else.
